newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV, KORDA REACH GERMAN GRASSCOURT FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV, KORDA REACH GERMAN GRASSCOURT FINAL.

text.p: Top-seeded Yevgeny Kafelnikov easily defeated former Wimbledon champion Boris Becker in the semifinals of the $875,000 Halle grasscourt tournament on Saturday.
Kafelnikov will now play the unseeded Petr Korda of the Czech Republic, who beat Dutchman Paul Haarhuis 7-6 6-4, in Sunday's final.
Kafelnikov, who ousted Germany's Michael Stich in the quarter-finals on Friday, crushed the fourth-seeded Becker 6-3 6-4 in a 75-minute match.
"It wasn't the Boris I've known before," said Kafelnikov, who said he felt like he was playing against the whole world because the crowd was almost entirely behind Becker.
"I had a horrible day today," said Becker, who was hampered by a weak serve and fell behind 5-0 after just 18 minutes.
"This was a painful result. For the fans I would have liked to have reached the final and won the tournament. But all in all I am satisfied. Everyone has black-out days like that."
The 23-year-old Kafelnikov had two chances to win the first set 6-0, but Becker managed to fight off the humilating sweep and held his serve before eventually falling 6-3.
"In the first set I felt like I wasn't there," Becker said. "Yevgeny has enough experience to take advantage of weaknesses like that. I still had a chance after that."
In the second set Becker was annoyed at several close calls that went in favour of the 23-year-old Russian and called an ATP supervisor to the court to complain about the decisions.
"When the calls were constantly going against you, you begin to lose faith," Becker said later.
It was the first match between the two men on a grass court. In five previous meetings, Becker had won four times.
Korda said he was delighted with his win over Haarhuis, but admitted his game would have to improve in Sunday's final against Kafelnikov.
"My performance today was okay, but it will have to be better to beat Yevgeny," Korda said.
